preamble.summary: Deuteronomy 28 contains the climactic blessings (vv. 1–14) and curses (vv. 15–68), the longest curse-list in the Torah. 4QDeutᵖ preserves vv. 15–18, 33–36, 47–52, and 58–62 — fragmentary but covering significant portions of the curse section.
preamble.notable_variants: No significant content variants in the preserved passages. The horror of the siege-cannibalism curses (vv. 53-57) is preserved as in MT — relevant background to Lam 2:20, 4:10 and Josephus' siege narratives.
preamble.scroll_condition: Fragmentary but with multiple distinct passages preserved.

variant_notes: The 'eagle from far away' curse (likely the Babylonians or, in later reception, the Romans) tracks MT.
